Subject: Security packaging ask — boundary schematics + SOC 2 mapping for Dedicated/Private

Karthik,

Thanks for the demo earlier — Lakeshore's InfoSec team has a couple of deliverables they need for procurement and our internal risk review. We need a concise packet that covers how Redwood separates customer workloads for Dedicated and Private deployments, plus the mapping to the SOC 2 network controls (and SIG/CAIQ pointers if available).

Specifically:
- A network schematic showing control-plane vs data-plane boundaries for both Dedicated (reserved GPU pools) and Private (VPC/on-prem) modes, labelled with firewall/egress choke points.
- A segmentation matrix that shows which services run in shared components vs per-tenant enclaves and how key material/KMS access is scoped.
- A control mapping CSV that ties those architecture elements back to common SOC 2 CC/SC items and SIG questions (we'll use it to accelerate our internal audit).

Target timeline: can you get a draft packet by EOD Monday PST? Procurement (Danielle) would like anything she can attach to the SOW.

Thanks — Priya
Priya Kaur
Head of InfoSec Programs, Lakeshore Health

Subject: Delivered: Control domain schematic + SOC 2 mapping (Lakeshore packet)

Priya / Lakeshore team — attaching the requested packet. Summary of what's included here:

- dedicated-private-boundary-diagram-v2.pdf (PDF, 3 pages) — annotated network schematic with control-plane/data-plane separation, egress anchors and sample ACL snippets.
- segmentation-matrix-annotated.xlsx (Excel) — row-per-component mapping that shows per-tenant vs shared services, KMS scoping, and expected ACLs.
- soc2-control-mapping.csv (CSV) — brief mapping between Redwood architecture elements and common SOC 2 CC/SC controls plus SIG/CAIQ references.

Key notes we call out in the packet:
- Dedicated pools: reserved GPU cohorts run in tenant-scoped compute clusters with network overlays that enforce tenant isolation. Control plane (cluster orchestration, model registry) is logically separated and accessible over a customer-isolated control channel; we include per-tenant identity boundaries enforced by IAM & mTLS.
- Private (VPC / on-prem): customers bring their network; Redwood services run inside customer-managed VPCs where KMS integration is optional (we provide HSM/KMS connectors). Data egress is blocked by default; explicit egress rules and audit logs are included per SOW.
- SOC 2 mapping: each architecture element is tied to the control narrative and the specific evidence artifact (logs, runbooks, architecture diagrams). Where a SIG/CAIQ question expects a configuration, we reference the location in the Drive folder.

Links & next steps:
- Drive packet: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2bExampleLinkDossier
- If this looks good, Ben and I can run a 30-minute walkthrough with Lakeshore's InfoSec next Wednesday (2027-10-06) to answer auditor questions.

Regards,
Karthik Iyer
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
